section_summary: This section records how Japanese foreign-currency bonds were treated during the war, including yen conversions, interest funds held in Japan, payments in Switzerland, and the status of French-franc bonds. It also contains correspondence with American bondholders seeking information about defaulted bonds, claims deadlines, and possible recovery. The Department generally offered to record holders’ information while declining to predict the terms of a future peace treaty.

subfiles.title: Edwin J. Paull’s bondholding information
subfiles.to: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: Paull reports two inherited Ujigawa Electric Power bonds and supplies his citizenship details.
subfiles.summary: Paull says he notified the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council and provides the bonds’ identifying information, his inheritance date, and his birth details.

subfiles.title: Reply to Edwin J. Paull
subfiles.about: The Department acknowledges receipt of Paull’s bond and citizenship information.
subfiles.summary: The Department will place Paull’s information in its records for possible future use.

subfiles.title: Japanese foreign-currency bonds
subfiles.from: Charles L. Hodge, United States Reparations and Restitution Delegation, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The delegation forwards Japanese Government information on wartime treatment of foreign-currency bonds.
subfiles.summary: Hodge summarizes interest funds held in Japan, conversion of dollar and sterling bonds into yen obligations, payments in Switzerland, and enclosed material on French bonds. Additional information was requested from the Japanese Government.

subfiles.title: How were Japanese bonds in foreign currency treated during the war?
subfiles.about: The report explains emergency interest arrangements and the 1943 conversion law.
subfiles.summary: It describes yen interest payments to Japanese and friendly-country holders, Swiss payments on specified sterling bonds, and deposits of other interest into a special account. It then outlines compulsory liquidation, conversion into yen bonds, and the Japanese Government’s assumption of remaining local and corporate bond liabilities. The report says a final postwar settlement depended on international agreement.

subfiles.title: Locations of bonds outside Japan converted into yen bonds
subfiles.about: Tables locate foreign-held Japanese government, municipal, and company bonds converted during the war.
subfiles.summary: The tables break down bond issues and face amounts by country and, for United States holdings, by state. They cover dollar and sterling government bonds, local bonds, and electric-power and other debentures, ending with totals.

subfiles.title: Balance of the Special Property Administration Account
subfiles.about: The schedule lists wartime interest balances for government, local, and debenture bonds.
subfiles.summary: It itemizes yen balances by issue and gives a grand total of about ¥69.64 million. Notes explain payment periods and exchange rates and identify an Osaka harbour-loan principal component.

subfiles.title: French-franc bond funds and payment schedule
subfiles.about: Schedules account for funds associated with the City of Tokyo’s French-franc bond compromise.
subfiles.summary: The schedules track sums received from Tokyo, funds held by banks, and principal and interest on old and new bonds through March 1948. Much of the numerical table is degraded in the OCR.

subfiles.title: Note on outstanding bond amounts
subfiles.about: A note qualifies the outstanding amount of a Tokyo electric-power bond issue.
subfiles.summary: It explains that an omitted amount remained outside completed wartime conversion procedures.

subfiles.title: Explanation of French-currency bonds outstanding
subfiles.about: The report explains the status of Japanese Government and City of Tokyo French-franc bonds.
subfiles.summary: It says French-currency bonds were exempted from the wartime dollar and sterling bond measures. For Tokyo’s 1912 issue, it recounts litigation over payment currency, suspension of remittances, and a 1939 compromise scheduled for execution in 1940. War conditions prevented execution, but Tokyo deposited funds with banks and stated its readiness to implement the agreement.

subfiles.title: Payment of foreign-currency bond interest in Switzerland
subfiles.about: The schedule records Swiss interest remittances for two sterling bond issues.
subfiles.summary: It lists payments on Japanese Government 1910 and Tokyo 1912 bonds and notes that payments were made through the Swiss Bank Corporation in Basel.

subfiles.title: Sterling bond obligations schedule
subfiles.about: The schedule asks for outstanding, redeemed, and converted sterling bond amounts and service funds.
subfiles.summary: Fragmentary tables cover government and local sterling loans, sinking-fund retirements, conversions into yen obligations, outstanding bonds abroad, and debt-service money deposited in Japan.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on George P. Hoke’s bonds
subfiles.about: A memorandum records James Hannah’s inquiry about George Hoke’s Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: It lists four bond holdings and their face amounts.

subfiles.title: Reply to James B. Hannah
subfiles.about: The Department discusses the current value and retention of Hoke’s bonds.
subfiles.summary: Matre says the bonds have no known present value, suggests retaining them, and explains the Department’s limited role concerning defaulted foreign securities.

subfiles.title: Charge slip for Hannah correspondence
subfiles.about: The slip tracks the Hannah bondholder file.
subfiles.summary: A filing and circulation record for the Hannah correspondence.

subfiles.title: Referral of H. H. Bloch’s letter
subfiles.from: Q. U. Sraleigh, Office of the Legal Adviser
subfiles.about: The Legal Adviser refers Bloch’s bond claim for action.
subfiles.summary: It encloses War Claims Act guidance for a reply.

subfiles.title: Duplicate referral of H. H. Bloch’s letter
subfiles.about: A second copy refers Bloch’s bond claim and War Claims Act guidance.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate referral concerning bonds guaranteed by Japan.

subfiles.title: Record-and-return routing slip
subfiles.about: The Legal Adviser requests recording and return of a document.
subfiles.summary: A brief record-and-return instruction.

subfiles.title: H. H. Bloch inquiry
subfiles.about: Bloch asks how to recover on Tokyo Electric Power Company bonds.
subfiles.summary: He says he held government-guaranteed bonds before the war and asks what claim action is available.

subfiles.title: Reply to H. H. Bloch
subfiles.about: The Department explains its policy and asks Bloch for bond and citizenship details.
subfiles.summary: Corliss describes the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council’s role, the inquiry about restoring cancelled mortgages, and uncertainty about a peace treaty. He offers to record Bloch’s holdings and encloses War Claims Act information.

subfiles.title: Jonathan H. Holmes inquiry
subfiles.about: Holmes asks whether his City of Yokohama bond can acquire value and whether a claim deadline might be extended.
subfiles.summary: He identifies a 1926 City of Yokohama bond and seeks advice after missing a claims period.

subfiles.title: Reply to Jonathan H. Holmes
subfiles.about: The Department explains its bondholder policy and the information it can record.
subfiles.summary: Corliss points Holmes to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, notes uncertainty about the peace treaty, and invites bond purchase and citizenship details for the Department’s records.

subfiles.title: Louise Hartford inquiry
subfiles.about: Hartford seeks advice after missing the claim deadline for her City of Yokohama bond.
subfiles.summary: She recounts the transfer of Yokohama Specie Bank assets to the Alien Property Custodian and asks about extension of the deadline, recovery of arrears and principal, and future Japanese payments.

subfiles.title: Hartford inquiry to Federal Reserve Bank
subfiles.to: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
subfiles.about: Hartford asks how to collect overdue interest on her Yokohama bond.
subfiles.summary: She identifies bond no. 16779 and asks about payments.

subfiles.title: Federal Reserve Bank reply
subfiles.from: R. R. Tompkins, Federal Reserve Bank of New York
subfiles.about: The bank advises Hartford to contact the bond’s paying agent.
subfiles.summary: It directs her to the paying agent.

subfiles.title: Hartford inquiry to Yokohama Specie Bank
subfiles.about: Hartford asks the paying agent about overdue bond interest.
subfiles.summary: She identifies her bond and requests payment instructions.

subfiles.title: New York Banking Department reply
subfiles.from: Edward Feldman, New York Banking Department
subfiles.about: The liquidator explains the disposition of Yokohama Specie Bank assets.
subfiles.summary: Feldman recounts the bank’s 1941 liquidation and transfer of bondholder-related funds to the Alien Property Custodian. He advises Hartford to inquire whether a claim can still be filed.

subfiles.title: Hartford inquiry to Office of Alien Property
subfiles.about: Hartford asks whether overdue interest can be paid and what action she should take.
subfiles.summary: She repeats her bond details and requests instructions.

subfiles.title: Office of Alien Property reply
subfiles.from: David L. Bazelon, Office of Alien Property
subfiles.about: The office states that the deadline for claims against vested City of Yokohama property expired.
subfiles.summary: Bazelon gives the August 8, 1948 deadline and refers other issues to the State Department.

subfiles.title: Reply to Louise Hartford
subfiles.about: The Department answers Hartford’s questions about her Yokohama bond.
subfiles.summary: Corliss says only the Office of Alien Property can address its filing deadline. He explains the Department’s limited assistance, refers her to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, and requests purchase and citizenship details for its records.

subfiles.title: Reply to Shigeto Inouye
subfiles.about: The Department explains the status of Inouye’s Tokyo Electric Light Company bonds.
subfiles.summary: Corliss says the bonds are in default and that a Treasury holdings census was not a claim filing. He suggests contacting the Office of Alien Property and the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, and asks for citizenship information before recording the holding.

subfiles.title: Shigeto Inouye inquiry
subfiles.about: Inouye asks about the status and interest payments of his Tokyo Electric Light Company bonds.
subfiles.summary: He mentions reporting the bonds to the Federal Reserve Bank and asks whether he must file a claim.

subfiles.title: Jonathan H. Holmes follow-up
subfiles.about: Holmes supplies citizenship and purchase details for his City of Yokohama bond.
subfiles.summary: He asks whether the bond needs an endorsement or citizenship certificate, identifies its purchase around December 1926, and encloses his birth certificate.

subfiles.title: Jonathan H. Holmes birth certificate
subfiles.about: A certified town record states Holmes’s birth date and place.
subfiles.summary: It records his birth on October 18, 1876, in Mattapoisett.

subfiles.title: Reply to Jonathan H. Holmes’s follow-up
subfiles.about: The Department says no bond endorsement or certificate is currently needed.
subfiles.summary: It will retain Holmes’s birth certificate and bond details.

subfiles.title: Louise Hartford’s bondholding details
subfiles.to: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: Hartford supplies purchase, payment, and citizenship details for her Yokohama bond.
subfiles.summary: She identifies bond no. 16779, its April 1927 purchase, last interest payment, and New York birth.
